summary: The coercivity, fixed-vertex compactness, boundary exclusion, differentiability, multiplier calculation, and terminal triangle facts are otherwise coherent, but the endpoint rank lemma is not established. Its asserted transition-count classification omits endpoint incidence possibilities, so the constraint qualification and KKT localization at a ray-vertex minimizer do not follow.
gaps: The finite case analysis leading to (9) is not exhaustive. A maximal chain of zero-weight pieces may itself contain one or more fan transitions, its two stops may occur on the same four-piece edge, and there may be additional fan-ray vertex transitions away from the two selected stops. The displayed counts 3+3, 3+1, and 1+1 count only the stops, yet the proof then allocates all remaining transitions as though these omitted possibilities had already been excluded. In particular, the claims that the ray-ray case must split as 2+2 and that every extra genuine vertex lies in one endpoint sector are asserted without a derivation. Thus the conclusion that every nonzero annihilator is an alternating triangle or a 3+3 pattern is unsupported.

Because the endpoint rank lemma is unproved, a nontriangular polygon with a fan-ray vertex has not been shown to have independent pullbacks of the active area, balance, and threshold constraints. The ordinary KKT step and the ensuing reduction to the two terminal triangle classes therefore leave the ray-vertex strata uncovered.
repair_hints: Give a complete incidence enumeration that tracks all six transitions, including transitions internal to every zero chain, coincident stop edges, and additional ray vertices, and prove from the edge moment equations and the supporting-line angular restriction that each nonlisted pattern is impossible before invoking KKT.
